title: Moving fixture unlock
summary: The left gripper starts around the handle of a free, hand-held fixture: a short channel with a ball inside, closed at its front by a spring-loaded latch gate, with a square socket on its side above the latch's push button. The left arm must grip the fixture and move it off its stand. While the fixture is still moving, the right arm must insert its peg into the socket, press the latch button down with the peg until the gate opens, and then pull the peg back out while the left hand keeps holding the fixture. The ball must then leave the fixture, run down a fixed inclined chute and come to rest in a basin at the chute's foot. The fixture must never be dropped.
robot_setup: Two Pandas facing each other along x. panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x), no tool: its tool frame is the gripper TCP (the point between the fingertips). It starts with the TCP at (-0.063, 0, 0.285), pointing straight down (TCP x = world +x, fingers closing along world y). Its fingers start open 0.0175 m each (0.035 m total aperture), straddling the fixture's 34 mm wide handle without gripping it. For this arm the finger servo is stiffer than the default (finger PD gains kp 1875 N/m and kd 8 instead of 300 and 12; the force is still capped at 15 N per finger). Its fingers also follow their own trajectory, not synchronized with the arm joints. panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). Its tool is a square peg, 16 x 16 mm in section and 70 mm long, hanging straight down from the tool frame: the tool frame is at the peg's top end and the tip is at tool-frame (0, 0, -0.07). A grey adapter (a horizontal bar from the hand and a short post) ends about 5 cm behind the peg on the hand side; peg and adapter form one rigid tool link. With the peg vertical the hand points straight down and the peg's top is 0.12 m ahead of the gripper TCP along tool x and 0.04 m below it. Start: tool frame at (0.12, 0.15, 0.40), peg vertical, rotated 180 deg about z (tool x = world -x), so the tip is at (0.12, 0.15, 0.33). Role labels per phase (left, right): moving_fixture_presentation: fixture_support, tracking_pin; relative_pin_insertion: moving_fixture_support, pin_inserter; mechanical_latch_open: fixture_support, latch_operator; follow_and_withdraw: outlet_operator, withdrawing_pin; gravity_delivery: outlet_support, cleared_pin.
scene: The fixture is a free rigid body, not attached to anything. At the start it rests level on a small orange stand plate carried by two thin grey posts. It is a blue channel running along x: a flat floor between two side walls 56 mm apart and 45 mm high. At its back (-x) end is a small handle block (16 mm along x, 34 mm wide, 28 mm tall). At its front (+x) end the floor stops short of the walls' ends, leaving an exit opening. An orange spring-loaded latch closes this exit with a 20 mm high gate standing just beyond the floor's end. The latch slides along the fixture's own vertical axis by up to 26 mm. Its push button sits right under a square socket (28 mm opening, 30 mm tall, 16 mm walls) that is fixed to the fixture beside the channel's front end on its +y side, above the wall. Pushing the button down lowers the gate below the floor and opens the exit, and a spring pushes the latch back up when released. An orange ball (radius 16 mm) lies loose on the channel floor behind the gate. Fixed in the scene are a grey inclined chute (an open channel, 66 mm wide inside, 22 mm walls) running downhill toward +x, and at its lower end a blue open basin (0.13 m along x by 0.12 m inside, 40 mm deep). Nothing moves by itself. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Fixture: free-root articulation. Its root link 'fixture' (mass 0.14 kg) is placed at reset at (0.02, 0, 0.26), unrotated, at rest; this start position is the reference for moving_fixture_presentation. In the fixture frame (origin on the channel floor's top surface): floor x in [-0.07, 0.02], |y| <= 0.028, top at z = 0; side walls at y = +-0.034 (12 mm thick, inner faces at +-0.028), x in [-0.068, 0.068], z in [-0.005, 0.045]; handle block x in [-0.091, -0.075], |y| <= 0.017, z in [0.011, 0.039]; socket: square ring with opening x in [0.006, 0.034], y in [0.051, 0.079] (axis at (0.020, 0.065)), z in [0.06, 0.09] (top face at z = 0.09). Latch link 'fixture_latch' (mass 0.025 kg): prismatic along fixture z, q in [-0.026, 0] m (q < 0 means pressed down), joint friction 0.04, damping 0.08. Its spring drive pulls toward q = 0 with stiffness 35 N/m, damping 0.2 and force limit 0.6 N; there is no other drive. Reset q = 0. Latch parts at q = 0, in the fixture frame: gate x in [0.020, 0.030], |y| <= 0.03, z in [0, 0.02]; connecting bar x in [0.017, 0.033], y in [0, 0.07], z in [0, 0.01]; button 22 x 22 x 16 mm centred (0.020, 0.065, 0.049) (top at z = 0.057, 3 mm below the socket). Stand: static plate 60 x 48 x 6 mm centred (0, 0, 0.247) (top at z = 0.25) on two posts at x = +-0.0195. Ball: radius 0.016 m, mass 0.025 kg, restitution 0.05, friction 0.2. At reset it is placed at rest at world (-0.008 + dx, dy, 0.277), with dx ~ U(-0.006, 0.006) drawn first and dy ~ U(-0.004, 0.004) drawn second (the only random draws; nothing is drawn later). That is fixture-local x about -0.028, 1 mm above the floor. Chute: static; its floor's top surface runs along the segment from (0.15, 0.13, 0.205) down to (0.33, 0.13, 0.08); 66 mm wide inside, 22 mm walls, friction 0.12. Basin: static open box, inner floor centre at (0.38, 0.13, 0.02), inside 0.13 (x) x 0.12 (y) m, 40 mm deep, friction 0.4. Announced `goal_target` = (0.06, 0.065, 0.335) (unused by the predicates). Peg tool: `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg, friction `tool_friction` = 0.3, restitution 0.05. Table friction `table_friction` = 0.08. `object_mass`, `radius`, `incoming_speed`, `fixture_speed`, `preview` and `restitution` are not used by this task. Horizon `horizon` = 25 s.

phases.name: moving_fixture_presentation
phases.text: the left gripper grips the fixture body (both left-arm fingers in contact with it; contact with the latch does not count), while the fixture's frame origin is more than 0.018 m away from where it started and the fixture's centre of mass moves faster than 0.005 m/s.

phases.name: relative_pin_insertion
phases.text: the peg is inserted into the socket while the fixture keeps moving, for 0.06 s without interruption. Measured in the fixture frame, the peg tip (tool-frame point (0, 0, -0.07)) is within 5 mm horizontally of the socket's axis and 10-35 mm below the socket's top face (insertion depth 0.01 m < depth < 0.035 m; the socket itself is 30 mm deep). Meanwhile the left gripper still grips the fixture body and the fixture's centre of mass moves faster than 0.003 m/s.

phases.name: mechanical_latch_open
phases.text: the latch is pressed down by more than 17 mm (latch joint q < -0.017 m) at a moment when the peg tool touches the latch.

phases.name: follow_and_withdraw
phases.text: the peg tip is more than 15 mm above the socket's top face, measured along the fixture's z axis only (depth < -0.015 m, any lateral position). At the same moment the peg tool does not touch the latch and the left gripper still grips the fixture body.

phases.name: gravity_delivery
phases.text: after this phase has begun, the ball touches the chute; a chute contact before this phase does not count. After that, the ball rests in the basin for 0.7 s without interruption. Rests means: in the basin's frame (origin at the inner floor centre) its centre is within 0.0528 m of the centre along both x and y (0.45 x radius inside a 0.06 m half-width square) and between 0.012 m and 0.0381 m above the floor; it has touched the basin within the last 25 ms; and its speed is below 0.09 m/s. This completes the task.

task_failures: fixture_grasp_drop: at any time, the fixture's frame origin (a point on the channel floor's top surface, 20 mm behind the floor's front edge) is below z = 0.18 m.
contact_rules: The fingers of either arm may touch the fixture body (channel, handle, socket) and the ball, but not the latch (gate, bar, button). The right peg tool (whole tool link, adapter included) may touch the fixture body, the latch and the ball. Nothing on either robot may touch the stand, the chute, the basin or the table. No other robot part (hand or arm links) may touch anything. The two arms and their tools may never touch each other, and no arm may touch itself.
world_goals_fixed: Drop limit: the fixture's frame origin must stay at or above z = 0.18 m.
world_goals_seeded: `goal_target` is announced at reset in the state. It is a fixed point, not seed-dependent: where the socket's mid-height centre would be if the fixture were moved 20 mm along +x from its start. No predicate uses it, but it gives away the fixture's location: privileged mode only. The ball's seeded start is not announced.
difficulty_note: The peg must go into a socket with about 6 mm clearance per side while the other arm is carrying that socket, then press the latch down and withdraw, all while the left hand keeps a finite-force grip on a free, cantilevered fixture. The delivery then needs the fixture's exit brought over the chute so that the ball reaches the chute only once the final phase has begun.
standard_notes: Nothing moves at t = 0: the fixture rests on its stand with the ball inside and the left fingers open around its handle. The latch springs back up toward closed whenever the peg stops pressing it.
